mentl/5dea3c4:
mentl query <file> "modules" projects the weave's module set from the
NModule cells driver_entry_with_ranges already mints per range — the
same cells module_path_of_span narrows by containment, read whole
instead. A graph read, not a second walk of the filesystem.

It exists because this session needed the answer and could not get it.
The driver proves the DAG on every invocation and could show it to
nobody, so "which modules does this entry pull" was answered by a
hand-written shell transitive-closure loop over grep '^import'. The
facet was born red against the prior pin (error: unknown query:
modules), and its frontier leg pins the count and two named members so
it cannot pass on a bare number. Its answers match the hand walk it
retires: canon 7, lower 22.

What that hand walk measured is worth more than the verb. Cost tracks
module count, not entry size: 17-line canon (7 modules) 0.75s, 3594-line
parser (13) 1.82s, 890-line driver (20) 3.47s, 6559-line lower (22)
4.48s — driver costs nearly twice parser on a quarter of the lines. Per
module it rises with the count: 0.107, 0.140, 0.174, 0.204 s/module.
Fitting a*N + b*N^2 on the endpoints gives 0.062*N + 0.0064*N^2, which
predicts parser at 1.89s against 1.82s measured. The compile is
quadratic in module count, and at 22 modules the quadratic term is ~69%.

The mechanism is structural and already named. driver_check_entry runs
infer_program_converged once per module, each against the shared env
every prior module installed into, so N lookups over an env that grows
with N. That is the env_find_flat class, whose fix is name-is-handle in
Phase 9.3. What is new is the tie: the wheel's own per-invocation cost
is bound to that peer by a fitted curve rather than a code reading.

This supersedes the four-pin hunt for a 0.28s constant in the prelude.
The constant stops mattering once the quadratic dominates.

stoop/5db05e1:
A panel was a heading, a body and a photo in fixed positions, which is a
form. A zine is what happens when somebody glues cuttings to a board at
whatever angle they land and photocopies the result, and the press could
not make one. It can now. A panel keeps its flowed text, which comes from
the desk and re-flows when the format changes, and gains a paste-up layer
of cuttings placed by hand: text in four voices, photographs, rules and
blocks, black on white or knocked out, dragged, resized, turned, stacked,
and undone all the way back.

Every cutting is held as a fraction of its panel rather than a measurement.
A panel is a different size in every format, and the one promise the press
already made is that changing the vessel retypes nothing; a collage stored
in points would have broken it. Fractions move with the panel, so the
suite's assertion that a paste-up survives a change of format is the same
assertion the flowed text already passed.

The ransom note cuts every character in a different face, size and tilt,
all derived from the character and its index rather than drawn at random,
so the letters sit in the same places on screen, on paper and on the
machine that opens the issue next week. Screen and PDF read one shared
description of the cut letters; deriving the jitter twice would have let
them drift apart. The first version read the hash with a signed shift and
handed half of all characters a negative face index, which the screen hid
and the PDF writer threw on.

It prints. The PDF writer draws each cutting at its true angle about its
own centre, with the four ransom faces and the hand voice registered as
standard Type 1 fonts and their real width tables, so a headline breaks
where it actually runs out of panel. A text cutting grows to hold its
words, measured from the layout the browser performed and written back to
the model, because a cutting that swallows a line is the same lie the fit
meter exists to stop.
